# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, and no safe operation is identifiable. I will wait for the Mute’s manual reading and the Deaf’s visual observations. 
``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display reads 0. Indicator light is red. Wires from left to right are 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The Deaf reports display 0, red indicator, and wire colours 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I still lack the manual’s rule identifying the safe wire, so I will ask the Mute for the relevant instructions. 
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="What manual rule applies to display 0, red indicator, and these wire colours? Which wire position is safe to cut?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent three gesture groups: group 1 is index-finger-up, index-finger-pointing sideways, index-finger-pointing sideways. Group 2 is index-finger-up, index-finger-up, index-finger-pointing sideways, index-finger-pointing sideways, index-finger-pointing sideways. Group 3 is index-finger-up, index-finger-up, index-finger-up, index-finger-pointing sideways.

The Deaf’s relay gives three gesture groups, but gestures are not meaningful to me directly, and their descriptions do not establish which wire is safe. I need the Mute to state the manual’s result in words rather than gesture groups. 
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please state plainly: for display 0, red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green, which wire position must I cut?")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one gesture group: five symbols total — first two are index-up gestures, followed by three V-sign gestures.

The Mute is still communicating only through gestures. I cannot see those gestures, so I am relaying the latest group descriptions back to the Mute and asking for an unambiguous wire number. 
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I received your fourth group as two index-up gestures followed by three V-sign gestures. I cannot see gestures. Please encode the safe wire as a single unmistakable gesture group or otherwise provide a direct wire number through Deaf.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one group: two V-sign gestures.

The latest two V-sign gestures still do not identify a wire position under any stated code. I will establish a simple unambiguous convention: the Mute should send exactly one, two, or three index-up gestures, with the count equal to the safe wire position. 
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please send exactly one, two, or three index-up gestures, with the number of gestures equal to the safe wire position. Use no other gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one group: one V-sign gesture.

The latest single V-sign is not the requested numeric encoding, so I still cannot safely identify a wire. I will ask the Mute to use distinct, countable symbols for positions 1, 2, or 3 and send only one of them. 
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer with exactly one symbol for the safe wire: thumbs-up means wire 1, V-sign means wire 2, or three-finger sign means wire 3. Send only that one symbol.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one group: two index-up gestures.

The latest relay is two index-up gestures. This matches the earlier agreed encoding in which the count of index-up gestures identifies the wire position. Therefore, the safe action is to cut wire 2.
``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The previous wire cut was correct; the bomb has changed. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 already cut, wire 3 green. Mute sent one V-sign gesture.

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb now shows display 0 with a yellow light; wire 2 is already cut, leaving blue wire 1 and green wire 3. The Mute’s V-sign does not tell me safely which remaining wire to cut, so I will request the answer in spoken words.
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="For the new state display 0 and yellow light, with wire 2 already cut and wires 1 blue and 3 green, please tell me plainly whether to cut position 1 or position 3.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No new message from Mute. Bomb remains: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

No new manual instruction has arrived, so cutting either remaining wire would be unsafe. I will signal the Deaf to obtain the Mute’s plain-language answer on the next round rather than guessing.
``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👉", "🤝"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one index-up gesture: ?. The bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

The Mute’s latest signal is still inaccessible to me as a gesture, and no wire choice has been stated plainly. Since wire 2 is already confirmed correct but the remaining choice is unresolved, I will ask the Mute directly for the position number.
``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please reply with the wire position as spoken words only: say exactly 1 or exactly 3. Do not use gestures.")
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived. I still cannot distinguish whether wire 1 or wire 3 is safe, so I will not guess.
``` 
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one index-up gesture: ?. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

The earlier two index-up gestures correctly identified wire 2, establishing that the number of index-up gestures is the wire position. The latest message is one index-up gesture, so the safe remaining wire is position 1.
``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
